units.name: 01 Say It Better
units.passage: Most people already know enough words to speak clearly and with style, even if their vocabulary is only average. In fact, the perfect word for a situation is probably sitting in your memory, ready to come out. The problem is that many of us get used to repeating a small set of familiar words. We call a mountain "big," a dress "pretty," and a movie "interesting" again and again, until the people listening to us start to lose interest. When we want to sound stronger, we simply put "very" in front: "very big," "very pretty," "very interesting." But there is no reason to accept such dull language. Rather than making a weak word longer with intensifiers like "very" or "really," pick a lively word that fits your meaning exactly. This makes your message sharper and easier to understand. For instance, if someone makes you extremely upset, you could say you are "furious" or "enraged" instead of just "angry." These words are not rare at all, yet they can give your conversations much more depth and color.

units.name: 02 Reviews Speak
units.passage: Today we can buy an almost endless number of products, and online reviews of them are everywhere. Many companies try to remove or hide bad reviews, but they may need to change their thinking about this. Researchers at the Spiegel Research Center studied product reviews and compared star ratings with how likely shoppers were to buy. Surprisingly, buyers were most willing to purchase not when a product had a perfect five-star score, but when its average was between 4.2 and 4.5. Perfect scores seemed less convincing because shoppers suspected they were too good to be true. This may sound strange, but negative reviews can actually help a product. They show that the opinions come from real, honest customers, and this creates trust. As a result, people who are thinking about buying can make a decision with a more balanced picture of the product. In the end, shoppers already understand that no single product can satisfy every person, so a few complaints make the ratings feel more believable.

units.name: 03 Are You Free?
units.passage: Real freedom can be reached only by choosing to limit yourself. Freedom does not mean doing anything you like; it means deciding what you are ready to give up. For example, you might get up earlier, keep your e-mail closed until the afternoon, or remove social media apps from your phone. You could also cut down on activities such as hanging out with friends, keeping them to only two or three days in a week, so more of your time goes to the things that really count. If you hope to build better study habits, hand something you treasure to a close friend and let them keep it if you fail to reach your study goals. Small sacrifices like these give you back time and attention, so you can concentrate on yourself. They also teach you that your time and focus have value in themselves. Setting limits is not a way of losing freedom; it is a way of taking control. Don't let distractions or the demands of others run your life. Take charge of it and focus on what matters most.

units.name: 04 Imprinting
units.passage: In our lives, there are special windows of time, called "imprinting" periods, when we can pick up certain skills with less effort. Learning a second language is one example, and abilities in music, such as writing or playing songs, also tend to develop most when a person is at a particular age. The teenage years, or puberty, are another powerful time, especially for building social skills and emotional intelligence. In this stage, young people become better at managing relationships, controlling their feelings, and understanding others as they think carefully about their own emotions. They can strengthen these abilities by taking part in group activities, listening actively to others, and meeting a wider range of people. Doing volunteer work and joining school clubs are helpful, too. When people learn at the proper time like this, they can reach their full potential and truly master certain skills. However, if they miss these chances, it is much more difficult to build such skills later in life. For this reason, we must notice these periods and use them well to open up better chances to learn and grow.

units.name: 05 TikTok
units.passage: Teenagers around the world are crazy about TikTok challenges. Have you ever felt proud after showing off a dance or joining a fun new trend? That feeling is the main reason so many people take part: approval from friends, tons of likes, and the excitement of getting attention. But there is a catch. Not every challenge is safe. Some are simply for fun, while others can be dangerous, such as eating extremely hot chili peppers or trying risky stunts. In fact, a lot of teens jump into these challenges without thinking about the danger, just because their friends are joining or because it seems thrilling. Now, what if things went the other way? Picture popular challenges that improve your health, build your confidence, or help you learn new skills instead of hurting you. TikTok could become a place for creativity and personal growth, not only a home for trends that disappear quickly. So the next time a viral challenge appears on your screen, stop and ask yourself whether it is really worth the danger or whether you could try something better instead.

units.name: 06 Born to Learn
units.passage: Improving at something can be difficult, particularly when you feel you are not moving forward at all. You may think you have hit your limit and cannot get any better. Many people believe that when their progress stops, they will soon start to go downhill. Athletes, for instance, are afraid of becoming weaker, and scientists worry that their thinking will get slower. However, growth almost never moves in a straight line. Being stuck is not a sign of failure, and reaching a peak does not mean there is nowhere higher to climb. Instead, such moments tell you that you may need to try a new approach. If your progress has stopped, maybe the road you chose is not right for you, your way of practicing is not effective, or you simply do not have enough energy. To move ahead, you sometimes have to step back and look for another way. The new road might feel strange or hard at first, but that uncomfortable feeling is often the point where true learning starts. Progress is not a straight highway; it bends, turns, and circles back.

units.name: 07 Greener, Greater!
units.passage: A lot of people assume that being kind to the planet is difficult. In their minds, it involves selling the family car, cutting back on what factories make, or putting expensive solar panels on the roof. But if we truly want a cleaner world, choosing green should be simple. Better still, it should happen automatically, so that people hardly need to think about it. These days, a growing number of technologies are built to guide us toward eco-friendly behavior with little or no effort. Take motion sensors, for example. They switch off the lights whenever a room is empty, so less electricity is wasted. In the same way, the heating and cooling system in an office can be set to run a bit cooler in winter and a bit warmer in summer on its own. Such a small adjustment can save a lot of money and protect the environment at the same time. In the end, tools like these can make a much bigger difference than simply asking people to remember to act green by themselves.

units.name: 08 How to Do Well
units.passage: Once people have practiced a sport like skiing or tennis for a while, their movements gradually become automatic. They begin to play almost without thinking, and they lose the ability to make careful, conscious changes. From this point on, more hours on the slope or the court do not make their actions more precise, and they do not sharpen the basic skills behind them. In other words, simply having more experience does not lead to better performance. With this limit in mind, let us consider how people who want to become experts grow their abilities. Unlike ordinary players, future experts keep getting better because they practice with clear focus. Their biggest task is to stay away from acting unconsciously, or doing things on autopilot. To fight against this danger, they keep setting fresh goals and raising their standards. As a result, they become faster and more accurate, and they gain greater control over what they do.

units.name: 09 A Life in Progress
units.passage: However steady you try to be, life will sometimes get in the way of your plans. You may catch a cold, take a business trip, or have to take care of something at home. Each time this happens, keep one easy rule in mind: never skip twice in a row. Missing a single day is fine, but return to your routine as soon as you can, or the break may grow into a bad habit. All of us have days when we feel tired or lazy, and that is not the real issue. The real issue is the popular idea that something done imperfectly has no value at all. In fact, even a "bad" workout is often the one that matters most for keeping a habit alive. A short, weak session still keeps your routine going, and that small effort moves you toward your goals and strengthens your self-control and confidence. So do something, even a little, and don't let one missed day wipe out the progress you have made.

units.name: 10 The Art of Humor
units.passage: Many jokes work because they break the usual rules of social life, but at what point does a joke stop being funny? Laughing at yourself is usually safe, yet making fun of other people calls for care. Friendly teasing gets people laughing and is based on warm feelings, while unkind teasing seems like an attack. Skilled comedians know that when listeners feel hurt, the joke was told badly; the audience is not to blame. One useful technique is irony, which means saying the reverse of what you actually mean to make people laugh. Imagine someone cuts you off while you are talking. You could say, "Oh, excuse me for talking during your interruption!" The contrast is what makes it funny. Exaggeration can also be effective if you use it with care. When a friend spells your name wrong, you might playfully reply, "That's it, our friendship is finished!" In the end, humor is meant to be enjoyable, not painful. Watch how people react, add some kind words to your jokes, and keep the atmosphere light.

items.exp: 유머는 상처가 아니라 즐거움을 줘야 하므로 반응을 살피고 친절한 말을 섞는 등 배려하며 써야 한다고 했어요.

units.name: 11 Pandemic
units.passage: During the past hundred years, people did a good job of stopping diseases like SARS in 2003, the H1N1 flu in 2009, and Ebola in West Africa from turning into worldwide disasters. Looking at this from the other side, however, we can ask: Did the long period without a global pandemic actually leave the world weaker against the next one? I believe it did. Until recently, hardly anyone expected a worldwide health emergency to change their daily lives. That is why so many were caught off guard when COVID-19 finally spread across the globe. The strange thing about peaceful times is that they give people a false feeling of safety and readiness, and they also make people doubt warnings. Experts had told us for years that global crises would come, but few listened. Many thought such dangers belonged only to the past or to faraway places. It is difficult to persuade people that they are in danger when they believe the problem has already been solved. Still, we must remember that having no danger today does not mean the risks are gone.

units.name: 12 Why Promises Matter
units.passage: Do you have a friend who rarely does what they say they will do? If someone keeps breaking small promises, like not showing up when you planned to meet, you gradually stop trusting them. The same thing happens when you break promises you make to yourself. At first, you might feel a little sorry, but over time it becomes harder to take your own goals seriously. Finally, you no longer trust yourself, and even simple tasks begin to feel too heavy. The good news is that you can rebuild this trust by keeping small promises, like eating healthy food for one day. This helps you behave the way you want to, which gives you a true feeling of control. Then you can face bigger challenges, such as keeping calm when you are angry or leaving a harmful relationship. All of this begins with one simple habit: take the promises you make to yourself as seriously as the ones you make to others. Keep your word, and you will be in charge of your life. It is up to you whether you trust yourself or keep letting yourself down.

units.name: 13 Learning Approach
units.passage: During my teacher training, my instructors kept repeating one simple rule: a fun teacher produces students who learn more. According to this idea, if every lesson felt as thrilling as a film, students would never lose interest in what they study. It is an attractive belief, but I think it misses the point. Instead of competing with movies, we can offer students tasks that have real meaning and that motivate them, and we can help them see that working through a hard problem brings a much greater sense of satisfaction in the end. Young people already have endless entertainment on their phones and screens. If our classes simply copy that kind of content, students will not develop a deep understanding or the critical thinking that they have a right to. Above all, nobody learns much by just sitting still and watching. Real learning happens when students roll up their sleeves and do the work themselves. In other words, learning must be an active process, not a passive one.

units.name: 14 Path to the Answer
units.passage: Long before the Internet, people relied on the encyclopedia in much the same way we rely on search engines now. Because answers were always close at hand, many people believed they did not have to think things through by themselves. The German philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer disagreed. In his view, a conclusion that you work out alone is worth a hundred times more than one you simply look up. He complained that people rushed to books too quickly rather than staying with their own ideas, and he suggested opening a book only after your own thoughts had run out. These days, clicking has taken the place of reading, and we often mix up data, information, knowledge, and wisdom as if they were the same thing. For Schopenhauer, information by itself was not very valuable; it was just a means of reaching insight. We can push his idea one step further: when we are buried under endless information, there is hardly any space left for careful thought. What fills our minds then is noise, not clarity, and while we are busy with the noise, we miss the music.

units.name: 15 Renaissance
units.passage: In the Renaissance, city-states were powered by a humanist idea: people could, and indeed should, go beyond the limits of what seemed possible. Thinkers of that age believed that great things were born when people questioned the way things had always been done. Michelangelo's painting on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel shows this clearly. Today we see him as the ideal choice for that project, but back then he did not look like one. He had made his name mainly as a sculptor rather than as a painter. Even so, Pope Julius II picked him, because he hoped Michelangelo would give the ceiling the depth and lifelike quality of sculpture. His marble statue David, finished in 1504, had already proven how well he understood the human body. Compare that attitude with our own. Nowadays we hand work only to people who have done it successfully before. Instead of seeing risk as a brave adventure, we try to escape it no matter what. It is hardly surprising, then, that our era is not a second Renaissance.

units.name: 16 Social Interactions
units.passage: Professor Jonah Berger compares people to atoms that keep bumping into one another. In his view, our contact with others never stops changing our identity and our behavior. Put simply, the people and things that surround us affect how we think and act every single day. Very often we come to like something not because it truly suits our taste, but only because it appears in front of us again and again. Think of people who see soda advertisements on TV all the time; they usually begin to connect those drinks with happy emotions. What matters more is that this effect is not limited to small likes and dislikes. It influences the whole course of our lives. Our surroundings form the way we think, and the way we think directs what we do. So if we take in better things, we will eventually get better results. For this reason, we should actively look for good ideas, smart choices, and people who motivate us. The more good influences you pick, the more your life will head the right way.

units.name: 17 Transition Period
units.passage: Dr. Arnett wanted to find out what being an adult really means, so he interviewed 300 young people between the ages of 18 and 29. To his surprise, none of them felt completely grown up; they all said they were somewhere in the middle. Arnett gave this period a name: "emerging adulthood." It is often a time full of instability and doubt, so how should we handle it? One piece of advice is to accept that life does not come with a clear map. During these years, our thoughts and moods swing back and forth more than at any other point in life, and we often doubt the decisions we make. This is perfectly natural. So instead of trying to plan every step, follow your interests and give new things a try. Doing so may feel strange in the beginning, but it can help you discover strengths you never knew you had, new passions, and even a direction that changes your life. Things may not turn out the way you expected, yet when you accept uncertainty, new doors begin to open.

units.name: 18 Stories for Children
units.passage: Young children tend to accept the stories they hear and read as true, so writers must think hard before giving a tale a sad or upsetting ending. A good story for children pays attention both to the young reader's feelings and to the realities of life. Such a story might show how things work in the real world, for instance how people overcome difficulties. It might also teach a lesson, offer comfort, give encouragement, or simply be fun. However, a story fails at every one of these goals if the child finishes it feeling disappointed and hopeless. For children, an unhappy ending is not just a matter of taste; it is a real problem. When a tale closes in sadness, a child may feel that nothing has been settled, and this can lead to confusion or frustration. That is why a children's story should end in a way that makes young readers trust that the characters will go on living happy, successful lives after the last page.

paid
items.exp: 슬픈 결말에서는 아무것도 '해결되지' 않은 느낌을 받는다는 뜻이므로 resolved와 가까워요.

items.q: 지문의 문장 '... end in a way that makes young readers [trust] that the characters will go on living ...'에서 [trust]가 동사원형으로 쓰인 이유로 알맞은 것은?
choices: trust가 명사로 쓰였기 때문에
앞에 조동사 should가 있기 때문에
사역동사 make의 목적격 보어이기 때문에
명령문이기 때문에
주어가 복수이기 때문에
items.exp: 'make + 목적어 + 동사원형' 구조로, 사역동사 make의 목적격 보어 자리에 원형부정사 trust가 쓰였어요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Write a Realistic Sad Story
Children Can Tell Truth from Fiction
Fun Is All a Children's Story Needs
The Long History of Fairy Tales
Why Children's Stories Need a Hopeful Ending
items.exp: 'a children's story should end in a way that makes young readers trust that the characters will go on living happy, successful lives'라며 희망적인 결말의 필요성을 말하는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, which is NOT mentioned as something a good children's story might do?
choices: show how people overcome difficulties
teach a lesson
make children read faster
offer comfort
simply be fun
items.exp: 'how people overcome difficulties', 'teach a lesson, offer comfort, give encouragement, or simply be fun'은 언급되지만 읽기 속도는 나오지 않아요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

For young readers, a sad ending is a serious (A) ___ rather than a matter of taste, so a children's story should leave them feeling (B) ___ about the characters' future.
choices: (A) problem — (B) worried
(A) problem — (B) hopeful
(A) choice — (B) hopeful
(A) joke — (B) curious
(A) lesson — (B) confused
items.exp: 'an unhappy ending is not just a matter of taste; it is a real problem'이라 했고, 아이들이 인물들이 행복하게 살 것이라 믿게(trust) 끝나야 한다고 했으니 problem과 hopeful이 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (However, a story fails at every one of these goals if the child finishes it feeling ___.)
choices: excited and curious
bored and sleepy
proud and confident
disappointed and hopeless
calm and relaxed
items.exp: 뒤에서 슬픈 결말은 'confusion or frustration'으로 이어진다고 했으니, 아이가 실망하고 희망을 잃은 채(disappointed and hopeless) 책을 끝내면 이야기가 실패한다는 흐름이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: the characters will go on living [miserable], successful lives
writers must think [hard] before giving a tale a sad or upsetting ending
how people [overcome] difficulties
an unhappy ending is not just a matter of [taste]
this can lead to confusion or [frustration]
items.exp: 아이들이 인물들이 '행복하고(happy)' 성공적인 삶을 이어 갈 것이라 믿게 해야 한다는 뜻이라 miserable은 어울리지 않아요. 원문은 'living happy, successful lives'예요.

units.name: 19 Handling Conflict
units.passage: After a fight, a misunderstanding, or a hurtful moment, many people keep their angry feelings for a long time. They wait for the other side to apologize first, and they think they can forgive only after that happens. However, this habit often makes a small problem grow into a serious one. Why? Deep down, we feel that showing we were right is worth more than our own happiness. If you want a calmer life, you need to see that happiness is more valuable than winning an argument. So, give up the fight and be the first to make contact. Allow other people to be right. That does not mean you are the one who is wrong. When you do this, your heart will feel lighter, and you will be more comfortable with yourself. The other person may also stop defending himself and start acting more gently. Even if he doesn't, it is fine. You will still be satisfied, because you know you tried your best to make the world a little warmer. Above all, you will find peace inside yourself.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 다툼 후에는 상대가 먼저 사과할 때까지 기다려야 한다.
논쟁에서는 근거를 들어 자신이 옳음을 증명해야 한다.
옳음을 증명하기보다 먼저 다가가 마음의 평화를 찾아야 한다.
상대가 친절해지지 않으면 관계를 정리하는 것이 좋다.
사소한 오해는 대화 없이 시간이 해결하게 두어야 한다.
items.exp: 행복이 논쟁에서 이기는 것보다 소중하니 싸움을 그만두고 먼저 연락하라(be the first to make contact)고 주장하고 있어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 많은 사람들은 상대가 먼저 사과해야 용서할 수 있다고 생각한다.
먼저 화해하려는 노력이 작은 문제를 큰 문제로 만든다.
다른 사람이 옳다고 인정하면 내가 틀렸다는 뜻이 된다.
먼저 다가가면 상대는 반드시 친절해진다.
상대가 변하지 않으면 노력한 의미가 없다.
items.exp: 사람들은 상대가 먼저 사과하기를 기다리고, 그 후에야 용서할 수 있다고 생각한다(they can forgive only after that happens)고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 다툼 후 나쁜 감정을 오래 간직하는 사람이 많다.
우리는 속으로 옳음을 보여 주는 것을 행복보다 중시한다.
먼저 다가가면 마음이 가벼워질 수 있다.
상대가 변하지 않아도 괜찮다.
먼저 다가가는 것은 결국 자신이 틀렸음을 인정하는 것이다.
items.exp: 다른 사람이 옳다고 인정해도 그것이 내가 틀렸다는 뜻은 아니라고(That does not mean you are the one who is wrong) 했어요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 make contact의 영영 풀이로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: to stretch your arm to take something
to try to communicate with someone
to leave a place quickly
to refuse someone's help
to speak in a louder voice
items.exp: 상대가 사과하기를 기다리지 말고 먼저 '연락하여 다가가라'는 뜻이므로 누군가와 소통하려 한다는 풀이가 알맞아요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
Deep down, we feel [that] showing we were right is worth more than our own happiness.
choices: This is the book [that] I bought yesterday.
[That] car over there is mine.
He was so tired [that] he fell asleep.
I know [that] she is honest.
The girl [that] lives next door is kind.
items.exp: 문장의 that은 feel의 목적어가 되는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사예요. 같은 쓰임은 know의 목적어절을 이끄는 that이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Let Go of Being Right, Find Peace Inside
How to Win Every Argument
Why the Other Person Should Apologize First
The Science Behind Our Anger
Avoid Difficult People at All Costs
items.exp: 'happiness is more valuable than winning an argument'라며 옳음을 증명하는 대신 먼저 다가가 'peace inside yourself'를 찾으라는 글이에요.

items.q: Why will you still be satisfied even if the other person does not change?
choices: Because you have proved that you were right.
Because the other person will apologize later.
Because you no longer have to see that person.
Because winning the argument makes you happy.
Because you know you tried your best to make the world a little warmer.
items.exp: 'You will still be satisfied, because you know you tried your best to make the world a little warmer'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Instead of waiting for an apology to prove we are (A) ___, we should reach out first, because inner peace is worth more than (B) ___ an argument.
choices: (A) right — (B) losing
(A) wrong — (B) winning
(A) kind — (B) avoiding
(A) right — (B) winning
(A) angry — (B) starting
items.exp: 'we feel that showing we were right is worth more than our own happiness'라는 습관을 버리고 'happiness is more valuable than winning an argument'임을 알라고 했으니 right와 winning이 알맞아요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [your heart will feel lighter]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (When you do this, your heart will feel lighter, and you will be more comfortable with yourself.)
choices: You will lose weight more quickly.
You will feel that you have lost the argument.
You will be free from heavy, angry feelings.
You will forget the other person completely.
You will become less careful about your words.
items.exp: 'keep their angry feelings for a long time'하던 사람이 싸움을 그만두고 먼저 다가가면 마음의 짐이 가벼워진다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: many people [keep] their angry feelings for a long time
Allow other people [being] right
they think they can forgive only after that [happens]
this habit often [makes] a small problem grow
you know you [tried] your best
items.exp: allow는 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사' 형태로 써요. 원문은 'Allow other people to be right'이므로 being은 틀려요.

units.name: 20 Searching for Creativity
units.passage: Resources that are in short supply are often the very things that make us act. Take time as an example. Many people think a lack of time kills creativity, but this is not true. A clock that keeps ticking can actually help us, because it makes us work with a sense of urgency and passion. Imagine a writer who believes he has lots of time. He will probably miss his deadlines and have trouble completing his book. Money works in a similar way. It is the second resource that we usually feel we lack. We like to think that if we could pay for everything we dreamed of, we would create far more and far better work. However, I have watched many artists lose their creative energy as soon as they had plenty of money saved. Money certainly gives some artists power and inspiration. But for each of them, there is another artist who grows lazy and too pleased with himself because of it. In short, having less can push us to create more.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 창의력을 키우려면 충분한 시간과 돈이 필요하다.
부족한 자원이 오히려 행동과 창의력을 이끌어 낸다.
마감 기한은 작가의 창의력을 해친다.
예술가는 돈보다 명예를 추구해야 한다.
시간 관리는 돈 관리보다 중요하다.
items.exp: 부족한 자원이 우리를 행동하게 만들고, 적게 가진 것이 더 많이 창작하게 한다(having less can push us to create more)는 것이 요지예요.

items.q: 글에 따르면, 시간이 많다고 믿는 작가에게 일어날 가능성이 높은 일은?
choices: 더 좋은 작품을 쓴다.
창작에 대한 열정이 커진다.
돈을 더 많이 번다.
마감을 놓치고 작품 완성에 어려움을 겪는다.
다른 작가들을 도와준다.
items.exp: 시간이 많다고 믿는 작가는 마감을 놓치고 책을 끝내는 데 어려움을 겪을 것(miss his deadlines and have trouble completing his book)이라고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 글쓴이는 시간 부족이 창의력의 적이라고 생각한다.
째깍거리는 시계는 긴박감과 열정을 줄 수 있다.
돈은 사람들이 흔히 부족하다고 느끼는 두 번째 자원이다.
글쓴이는 돈이 생기자 창작 의욕을 잃은 예술가들을 보았다.
돈에서 힘과 영감을 얻는 예술가도 있다.
items.exp: 시간 부족이 창의력을 죽인다는 생각은 사실이 아니라고(this is not true) 했어요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 단어의 영영 풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: urgency: the need to deal with something quickly
deadline: a time by which something must be finished
inspiration: something that gives you new ideas
lazy: not wanting to work or make an effort
plenty: a very small amount of something
items.exp: plenty는 '충분한 양, 많음'이라는 뜻이라서 '아주 적은 양'이라는 풀이는 틀렸어요.

items.q:
다음 문장에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
We like to think that if we [could pay] for everything we dreamed of, we [would create] far more and far better work.
choices: 과거에 실제로 일어난 일을 나타낸다.
미래에 반드시 일어날 일을 나타낸다.
현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거이다.
could는 '허락'의 의미로 쓰였다.
far는 '먼'이라는 뜻의 형용사로 쓰였다.
items.exp: if + 주어 + 과거형(could pay), 주어 + would + 동사원형(would create)은 현재 사실과 반대되는 일을 가정하는 가정법 과거예요. far는 비교급을 강조하는 부사예요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Artists Need More Money
Time Management for Busy Writers
The Lives of Famous Artists
Having Less, Creating More
How to Save Money for Your Dreams
items.exp: 시간과 돈이 부족한 것이 오히려 우리를 행동하게 하며 'having less can push us to create more'라고 한 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, what can plenty of money do to some artists?
choices: It can make them work harder than ever.
It can make them lazy and too pleased with themselves.
It can help them meet every deadline.
It can give them more time to travel.
It can make them more humble.
items.exp: 'there is another artist who grows lazy and too pleased with himself because of it'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Although people believe that having more time and money leads to better work, a (A) ___ of these resources can actually (B) ___ us to create.
choices: (A) shortage — (B) stop
(A) supply — (B) push
(A) shortage — (B) push
(A) waste — (B) allow
(A) plenty — (B) force
items.exp: 'Resources that are in short supply are often the very things that make us act'와 'having less can push us to create more'에서 부족(shortage)이 창작을 밀어붙인다(push)는 요지를 알 수 있어요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (Resources that are in short supply are often the very things that ___.)
choices: make us act
waste our time
cost the most
hold us back
please everyone
items.exp: 이어서 째깍거리는 시계가 'makes us work with a sense of urgency and passion'이라 했으니 부족한 자원이 우리를 행동하게(make us act) 만든다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: Many people think a lack of time [kills] creativity
He will probably [miss] his deadlines
the second resource that we usually feel we [lack]
Money certainly gives some artists power and [inspiration]
having [more] can push us to create more
items.exp: 글 전체가 부족함이 창작을 이끈다는 내용이므로 마지막 문장은 'having less can push us to create more'여야 해요. more는 문맥과 반대예요.

units.name: 21 The Million-Dollar Question
units.passage: Back in the 1950s, I had a job in the shipping business, and the situation was terrible. Expenses kept climbing, goods arrived late, and many believed that trade by sea had no future. My team tried everything. We worked to build faster ships, cut fuel use, and hire fewer sailors. None of these efforts helped, and our expenses continued to grow. Then an outside expert asked us one basic question: "What can we do to lower shipping costs?" Until then, we had looked only at ships on the ocean. His question made us study the entire system. Soon we saw that the true problem was not the voyage. It was the time spent putting cargo on and taking it off, because every day in a harbor cost us money. The answer was to get the cargo ready before the ship came in. So we developed container ships as well as roll-on roll-off vessels, and loading became quicker and cheaper. Shipping costs fell by 60%, time in port dropped by 75%, and our business grew fast. When you view a problem more widely, you can discover a better answer.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 배의 속도를 높이는 것이 비용 절감의 핵심이다.
외부 전문가의 조언은 항상 따라야 한다.
해운업은 사라질 위기에 있다.
작은 문제부터 하나씩 해결해야 한다.
문제를 더 넓게 바라보면 더 나은 해결책을 찾을 수 있다.
items.exp: 마지막 문장에서 문제를 더 넓게 보면 더 나은 답을 찾을 수 있다(When you view a problem more widely, you can discover a better answer)고 주장해요.

items.q: 글에 따르면, 해운 비용 문제의 진짜 원인은?
choices: 배의 느린 속도
높은 연료비
항구에서 화물을 싣고 내리는 데 걸리는 시간
너무 많은 선원 수
바다의 거친 날씨
items.exp: 진짜 문제는 항해가 아니라 화물을 싣고 내리는 데 드는 시간(the time spent putting cargo on and taking it off)이었다고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 1950년대에는 많은 사람이 해상 무역에 미래가 없다고 여겼다.
글쓴이의 팀은 선원 수를 늘려 문제를 해결하려 했다.
외부 전문가의 질문 덕분에 전체 과정을 살펴보게 되었다.
새로운 배를 도입하자 화물 싣기가 더 빠르고 저렴해졌다.
항구에 머무는 시간이 75% 줄었다.
items.exp: 팀은 선원을 더 적게 고용하려고(hire fewer sailors) 했지, 늘리려 한 것이 아니에요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 cargo와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: crew
harbor
voyage
goods
fuel
items.exp: cargo는 배에 싣는 '화물'이라서 '상품, 물건'을 뜻하는 goods와 의미가 가장 가까워요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
None of these efforts helped, and our expenses continued [to grow].
choices: She wants [to grow] vegetables in her garden.
He went to the store [to buy] milk.
I have a lot of homework [to do].
She was happy [to hear] the news.
He grew up [to be] a doctor.
items.exp: continued to grow의 to grow는 continued의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사적 용법이에요. wants의 목적어인 to grow도 같은 쓰임이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Rise and Fall of Sea Trade
Ask a Bigger Question, Find a Better Answer
How to Build Faster Ships
Why Outside Experts Cost Too Much
A Sailor's Life in the 1950s
items.exp: 'What can we do to lower shipping costs?'라는 근본적인 질문이 전체 시스템을 보게 했고, 'When you view a problem more widely, you can discover a better answer'가 결론이에요.

items.q: What was the solution the writer's team finally found?
choices: Getting the cargo ready before the ship came in.
Hiring more experts from outside.
Building much larger harbors.
Sailing only in good weather.
Lowering the price of the goods.
items.exp: 'The answer was to get the cargo ready before the ship came in'이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The shipping team solved its cost problem not by improving the ships themselves but by looking at the (A) ___ system, which showed that time in (B) ___ was the real issue.
choices: (A) whole — (B) storms
(A) old — (B) port
(A) whole — (B) port
(A) fuel — (B) factories
(A) small — (B) offices
items.exp: 'His question made us study the entire system'이라 했고, 진짜 문제는 'every day in a harbor cost us money'라는 항구에서의 시간이었으니 whole과 port가 알맞아요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [His question made us study the entire system]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Until then, we had looked only at ships on the ocean. His question made us study the entire system.)
choices: We started to study how to become shipping experts.
We decided to build an entirely new company.
We kept looking only at the ships on the ocean.
We paid the expert to solve the problem for us.
We began to look at every part of the shipping process, not just the voyage.
items.exp: 그 전에는 'only at ships on the ocean'만 보았지만, 질문 덕분에 항해뿐 아니라 화물을 싣고 내리는 과정까지 전체를 살펴보게 되었다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: many [believed] that trade by sea had no future
our expenses [continued] to grow
every day in a harbor [cost] us money
the time [spending] putting cargo on and taking it off
loading [became] quicker and cheaper
items.exp: time은 '쓰이는' 대상이므로 과거분사 spent가 time을 꾸며야 해요. 원문은 'the time spent putting cargo on and taking it off'예요.

units.name: 22 Texting Instead of Talking
units.passage: Ghosting means rejecting someone without a word. It is a way to end a relationship without actually explaining to the other person that you want to stop seeing them. This behavior has existed for a long time, but today, thanks to so many online connections, it is easier than ever to avoid people. Is that really a positive change? Some experts see it as proof that many people now find it harder to deal with uncomfortable talks. Online messages are so easy to send that a lot of people text or email rather than meet and talk in person. However, talking face-to-face has many benefits. Our faces, hand movements, and voices can express feelings that written words cannot, even when we add emojis. When people talk in person, they understand each other more deeply, especially about difficult subjects. Meeting in person may be harder, but it is more likely to bring good results and help us grow as people.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 어려운 대화일수록 직접 만나 이야기하는 것이 좋다.
이별은 문자로 알리는 것이 예의이다.
이모티콘을 활용하면 감정을 충분히 전할 수 있다.
디지털 소통은 인간관계를 더 깊게 만든다.
불편한 대화는 피하는 것이 마음 건강에 좋다.
items.exp: 직접 만나는 것이 더 어렵지만 좋은 결과와 성장을 가져올 가능성이 크고, 특히 어려운 주제일수록 서로를 깊이 이해하게 된다고 주장해요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 고스팅은 최근에 처음 생긴 현상이다.
모든 전문가는 고스팅을 긍정적으로 본다.
이모티콘을 쓰면 문자로도 표정만큼 감정을 전달할 수 있다.
직접 대화는 쉽기 때문에 좋은 결과를 낸다.
많은 사람이 편리함 때문에 직접 대화 대신 문자나 이메일을 택한다.
items.exp: 온라인 메시지는 보내기가 아주 쉬워서 많은 사람이 직접 만나기보다 문자나 이메일을 보낸다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에서 직접 대화의 장점으로 언급되지 않은 것은?
choices: 표정과 손동작으로 감정을 전할 수 있다.
목소리로 글이 전하지 못하는 감정을 표현할 수 있다.
서로를 더 깊이 이해할 수 있다.
시간과 비용을 절약할 수 있다.
사람으로서 성장하는 데 도움이 된다.
items.exp: 표정·손동작·목소리, 깊은 이해, 좋은 결과와 성장은 언급되었지만 시간과 비용 절약은 나오지 않아요. 오히려 직접 만나는 것이 더 어렵다고 했어요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 ghosting의 의미로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: telling someone a scary story
sending many messages to a friend
ending a relationship by cutting off contact without explaining why
meeting someone in person to say goodbye
pretending to be someone else online
items.exp: 고스팅은 말 한마디 없이, 그만 만나고 싶다는 설명도 없이 관계를 끝내는 것이라고 지문 첫 부분에서 설명해요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
Online messages are so easy to send [that] a lot of people text or email rather than meet and talk in person.
choices: I think [that] he is right.
The box was so heavy [that] I couldn't lift it.
This is the house [that] Jack built.
[That] is my bag.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Ghosting: A Brand-New Problem
How Emojis Changed Our Feelings
Why Online Messages Are Always Better
The Rules of Online Friendship
Face-to-Face Talks: Harder but Worth It
items.exp: 'Meeting in person may be harder, but it is more likely to bring good results and help us grow as people'가 글의 핵심이에요.

items.q: How do some experts view the rise of ghosting?
choices: As a sign that people have become more honest.
As a positive change in modern relationships.
As a result of having too few online connections.
As proof that many people now find uncomfortable talks harder to handle.
As a problem that only teenagers face.
items.exp: 'Some experts see it as proof that many people now find it harder to deal with uncomfortable talks'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Although ghosting has become (A) ___ thanks to online connections, meeting in person communicates feelings better and helps us (B) ___ as people.
choices: (A) easier — (B) grow
(A) easier — (B) fail
(A) rarer — (B) grow
(A) harder — (B) relax
(A) kinder — (B) change
items.exp: 'it is easier than ever to avoid people'라 했고, 직접 만나는 것이 'help us grow as people'이라 했으니 easier와 grow가 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (Our faces, hand movements, and voices can express feelings that ___, even when we add emojis.)
choices: everyone already knows
written words cannot
we want to hide
only experts understand
last for a long time

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: Ghosting means [rejecting] someone without a word
it is easier than ever to [avoid] people

they understand each other more [deeply]

units.name: 23 Follow the Herd
units.passage: People sometimes use the word "sheeple" for those who copy the crowd without asking any questions. The word makes it sound as if nothing is worse than being a sheep that simply goes wherever the others go. But think about it. Have you ever followed someone else's lead? Almost everyone has. You have surely picked a product, a way of living, or an opinion because another person recommended it. Let's admit the truth: all of us have followed the herd at some time. And there is a good reason for this. Going along with others can make us feel that we belong. Also, fighting the group all the time is tiring. Nobody can question every single thing, and it isn't always helpful anyway. Besides, rejecting the crowd without thinking is no less blind than copying it without thinking. What matters is knowing when following the crowd is a sensible choice, and then doing it on purpose and with awareness.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 대중을 따르는 것은 언제나 어리석다.
모든 것에 의문을 품어야 한다.
유행하는 제품은 사지 않는 것이 좋다.
언제 대중을 따를지 판단하고 의식적으로 따라야 한다.
리더가 되려면 다른 사람과 달라야 한다.
items.exp: 중요한 것은 대중을 따르는 것이 현명한 때를 알고 의도적으로, 인식하며 따르는 것(What matters is knowing when ...)이라고 주장해요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 'sheeple'은 신중하게 판단하는 사람을 칭찬하는 말이다.
대부분의 사람은 다른 사람의 추천으로 무언가를 선택한 적이 있다.
다른 사람을 따르면 소속감을 잃게 된다.
집단에 계속 맞서면 힘이 난다.
생각 없이 순응을 거부하는 것은 현명한 행동이다.
items.exp: 다른 사람이 추천해서 제품이나 생활 방식, 의견을 고른 적이 분명 있을 것이고 거의 모든 사람이 그렇다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에서 대중을 따르는 것을 옹호하는 근거로 언급되지 않은 것은?
choices: 소속감을 느끼게 해 준다.
항상 집단에 맞서는 것은 지치는 일이다.
대중의 선택은 대체로 정답이다.
누구도 모든 것에 의문을 품을 수는 없다.
모든 것을 의심하는 것이 늘 도움이 되는 것은 아니다.
items.exp: 소속감, 피곤함, 모든 것을 의심할 수 없다는 점은 나오지만 대중의 선택이 대체로 옳다는 말은 없어요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 sensible과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: wise

careless
popular

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
[Going] along with others can make us feel that we belong.
choices: She is [going] to school now.
Look at the [sleeping] baby.
I saw him [running] in the park.
[Walking] down the street, I met Tom.
[Reading] books is my hobby.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Following the Crowd: Do It with Your Eyes Open
Why Sheep Make Wonderful Pets
Never Trust Other People's Opinions
The Loneliness of Being Different
How Advertising Controls Our Minds
items.exp: 'What matters is knowing when following the crowd is a sensible choice, and then doing it on purpose and with awareness'라며 의식적으로 따르라는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, what kinds of things have people chosen because someone else recommended them?
choices: A friend, a teacher, or a leader.
A book, a movie, or a song.
A product, a way of living, or an opinion.
A country, a city, or a neighborhood.
A hobby, a sport, or a club.
items.exp: 'You have surely picked a product, a way of living, or an opinion because another person recommended it'이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Since everyone follows others at times and doing so has real (A) ___, the key is to follow the crowd (B) ___, knowing when it makes sense.
choices: (A) benefits — (B) blindly
(A) dangers — (B) consciously

Following others makes us feel sleepy.
We should fight the group even harder.
Always going against others uses up a lot of our energy.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: those who [copy] the crowd without asking any questions
all of us [has] followed the herd at some time
Have you ever [followed] someone else's lead

units.name: 24 No Time Like Now
units.passage: The expression "pay the piper" means to pay for the fun you have had or to accept what happens because of your actions. Most people think it is from an old story from the Middle Ages, the Pied Piper of Hamelin. In the story, a man played his pipe and led all the rats out of the town, but the townspeople would not give him his money. To punish them, he played his music again, and this time the children followed him away. So the phrase tells us that sooner or later, we will face the results of careless or selfish behavior. When you run away from your duties now, the problems do not vanish. Instead, they wait for you and grow more difficult to solve. Eventually, your Future Self must carry the weight of today's decisions. However, if you act responsibly now, even a little, you prepare a brighter future for yourself. For instance, if you don't study today, your Future Self will have a hard time on test day. But if you open your books, even for a short time, the Future You will be grateful.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 전설 속 이야기는 믿을 필요가 없다.
약속한 돈은 반드시 지불해야 한다.
지금 책임을 다하면 미래의 자신이 혜택을 본다.
시험 기간에는 무리하게 공부하지 말아야 한다.
미래보다 현재의 즐거움이 더 중요하다.
items.exp: 오늘 책임을 피하면 미래의 자신이 부담을 지고, 조금이라도 책임을 다하면 더 밝은 미래를 준비할 수 있다는 것이 요지예요.

items.q: Pied Piper 이야기에 대한 내용으로 일치하는 것은?
choices: 피리 부는 사나이는 마을의 아이들을 구했다.
마을 사람들은 약속대로 돈을 지불했다.
이 이야기는 현대에 만들어졌다.
사나이는 피리로 쥐를 마을로 불러들였다.
사나이는 돈을 받지 못하자 음악으로 아이들을 데려갔다.
items.exp: 마을 사람들이 돈을 주지 않자 사나이는 벌을 주려고 다시 음악을 연주했고, 아이들이 그를 따라갔다고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 책임을 피하면 문제는 시간이 지나며 저절로 사라진다.
pay the piper는 행동의 결과를 받아들인다는 뜻이다.
미래의 자신이 오늘 내린 결정의 무게를 지게 된다.
조금이라도 지금 책임 있게 행동하면 더 나은 미래를 준비할 수 있다.
짧게라도 공부하면 미래의 자신이 고마워할 것이다.
items.exp: 책임을 피해도 문제는 사라지지 않고(the problems do not vanish) 기다렸다가 더 해결하기 어려워진다고 했어요.

items.q: 지문에 쓰인 vanish와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: appear
disappear
increase
return
explode

items.q:

The townspeople would not give him his money.

The townspeople would not give his money to him.
The townspeople would not give to him his money.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The True History of Hamelin
How to Get Rid of Rats
Pay the Piper: Your Future Self Is Watching
Why Tests Are Unfair to Students
Music That Changed the World
items.exp: 'pay the piper'라는 표현을 통해 'your Future Self must carry the weight of today's decisions'라며 지금 책임을 다하라고 하는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, where do most people think the expression 'pay the piper' comes from?
choices: A modern song about a traveling musician.
A famous test given in schools.
A saying used by rat catchers today.
A letter written by a town leader.
An old story from the Middle Ages about the Pied Piper of Hamelin.
items.exp: 'Most people think it is from an old story from the Middle Ages, the Pied Piper of Hamelin'이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The story of the Pied Piper reminds us that avoiding our duties now only makes problems (A) ___, so acting responsibly today is a (B) ___ to our future selves.
choices: (A) bigger — (B) burden
(A) bigger — (B) gift
(A) smaller — (B) gift
(A) disappear — (B) warning
(A) fun — (B) debt
items.exp: 미룬 문제는 'grow more difficult to solve'하고, 지금 책임 있게 행동하면 'you prepare a brighter future for yourself'라 했으니 bigger와 gift가 알맞아요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [your Future Self must carry the weight of today's decisions]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Eventually, your Future Self must carry the weight of today's decisions.)
choices: You will later have to deal with the results of what you choose now.
You will become physically stronger in the future.
Your decisions today will be forgotten tomorrow.
Other people will solve your problems later.
You should make fewer decisions every day.
items.exp: 'sooner or later, we will face the results of careless or selfish behavior'라고 했듯, 오늘의 선택이 낳은 결과를 미래의 자신이 감당해야 한다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: led all the rats [out] of the town
To [punish] them, he played his music again

units.name: 25 Hotter Than Ever
units.passage: The world is facing a serious climate emergency, but many national leaders still put money and business ahead of the health of the Earth. Scientists have explained again and again what will happen if nobody acts. Young campaigners such as Greta Thunberg have said that people in the future will not forgive anyone who chose to stay passive. As their demands become stronger, some adults simply ignore them. These critics argue that teenagers are not old enough to understand how society really runs, how complicated politics is, or what the economy needs. Some leaders even say that staying hopeful matters more than worrying. But isn't worry a natural reaction to danger? The young people raising their voices are the ones who will have to deal with the results, while those with power keep putting off real action. This unfair situation proves that we should listen to young people even more carefully, because the future planet will belong to them. They will not keep quiet while adults take risks with the world they will live in.

choices: 기후 문제보다 경제 성장을 먼저 해결해야 한다.

items.exp: 비판자들은 십 대가 사회가 돌아가는 방식, 복잡한 정치, 경제가 필요로 하는 것을 이해할 만큼 나이가 들지 않았다고 주장해요.

units.name: 26 Why This Luck?
units.passage: Several famous discoveries in history, including Newton's law of gravity and Archimedes' principle, came about by chance. People call this kind of lucky surprise "serendipity." Horace Walpole, a British politician and writer, created the word after he read a story called The Three Princes of Serendip. In the tale, the princes kept finding precious things while they were looking for something different. However, serendipity is more than simple good luck. It depends on staying in motion. The princes did not make their discoveries by resting in one place. Instead, they traveled, paid close attention, and connected with the world around them. Many big discoveries happen this way. For example, a shepherd who was searching for a missing goat came across the Dead Sea Scrolls, precious ancient Jewish writings. People who keep moving, watching carefully, and asking questions are the ones who find surprises. According to an old Spanish saying, a dog that moves quickly is the one that discovers a bone. Whether in a lab or in everyday life, success comes to people who do not stop. So keep exploring, because your next big discovery could be very close.

units.name: 27 Fidgeting
units.passage: Imagine you are in a classroom, listening to a lesson. Suddenly you realize that you have been twirling your pencil, drumming your fingers on the desk, or bouncing your leg, and you never even noticed. These small habits are known as fidgeting. Many people think of them as impolite or as proof that someone is not concentrating. However, fidgeting is a normal behavior, and people often judge it wrongly and too harshly. Human bodies are designed to move. When we stay in a chair for hours while trying to focus on a talk, our bodies make tiny movements to use up leftover energy and burn more calories. Actually, fidgeting may support our attention instead of hurting it. According to some research, people who fidget remember more information than people who stay still. Constant small motions appear to wake up the brain and help it absorb new facts. Therefore, considering these possible advantages, you shouldn't force yourself to stop fidgeting completely. Rather than fighting it, accept that it is often just your body's natural way of responding.

units.name: 28 Confidence and Belief
units.passage: People tend to trust a statement much more when the speaker sounds certain. But sounding confident is not the same as being correct. Some people who know very little can still seem completely sure. This happens because they are unaware of the limits of their own knowledge. For example, a child who was never corrected may become an adult who thinks he or she is never wrong and talks with total certainty. Also, a successful person who is always surrounded by fans can grow too proud. As a result, that person may say even very silly things in a perfectly confident voice. For these reasons, we should not accept information simply because it is spoken confidently. Rather than being moved by powerful words, we need to pause, check whether the facts are true, ask where the information came from, and pay attention to real experts instead of people who just have bold opinions. Today, false information travels fast, so this careful attitude matters more than ever.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 정보를 전달할 때는 항상 자신감 있게 말해야 한다.
성공하려면 주변에 지지자가 많아야 한다.
어릴 때부터 자신감을 길러 주는 것이 중요하다.
자신감 있게 말한 정보라고 해서 무조건 믿어서는 안 된다.
전문가보다 대담한 의견을 가진 사람이 더 믿을 만하다.
items.exp: 자신 있게 말해졌다는 이유만으로 정보를 받아들여서는 안 된다(we should not accept information simply because ...)는 것이 글의 핵심이에요.

items.q: 글에 따르면, 아는 것이 거의 없는 사람이 확신에 차 보일 수 있는 이유는?
choices: 다른 사람보다 많이 공부했기 때문에
자기 지식의 한계를 알지 못하기 때문에
항상 사실을 확인하기 때문에
전문가의 말을 자주 듣기 때문에
잘못된 정보를 싫어하기 때문에
items.exp: 그들은 자기 지식의 한계를 알지 못하기(unaware of the limits of their own knowledge) 때문이라고 했어요.

items.q: 글쓴이가 정보를 대할 때 하라고 권하지 않은 것은?
choices: 잠시 멈추고 생각하기
사실이 맞는지 확인하기
정보가 어디서 왔는지 묻기
진짜 전문가의 말에 귀 기울이기
자신의 대담한 의견을 더 강하게 말하기
items.exp: 멈추기, 사실 확인, 출처 묻기, 전문가에게 주의 기울이기는 언급됐지만, 대담한 의견만 가진 사람 대신 전문가를 따르라고 했으므로 대담한 의견을 내라는 말은 없어요.

items.q:
밑줄 친 단어의 문맥상 의미로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Today, false information [travels] fast, so this careful attitude matters more than ever.
choices: spreads
takes a trip
disappears
changes
slows down
items.exp: travels는 여기서 잘못된 정보가 빠르게 '퍼진다'는 뜻으로 쓰였어요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]에 대한 설명으로 알맞은 것은?
Rather than [being moved] by powerful words, we need to pause ...
choices: 현재진행형으로, '지금 움직이고 있다'는 뜻이다.
어법상 to be moved로 고쳐 써야 한다.
동명사의 수동형으로, '(강한 말에) 휘둘리는 것'이라는 뜻이다.
능동형 moving으로 바꿔도 의미가 같다.
주어 we와 상관없는 독립분사구문이다.
items.exp: being moved는 'being + p.p.' 형태의 동명사 수동형으로, 우리가 강한 말에 '마음이 움직이는[휘둘리는] 것'을 뜻해요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Speak with Confidence
Why Fans Love Successful People
Raising Children Who Never Doubt Themselves
The Speed of Modern News
Sounding Sure Is Not Being Right
items.exp: 'sounding confident is not the same as being correct'라며 자신감 있게 말한 정보라도 확인해야 한다는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, what may happen to a child who was never corrected?
choices: He or she may become an adult who thinks he or she is never wrong.
He or she may become a real expert.
He or she may stop talking to other people.
He or she may be surrounded by fans.
He or she may learn to check facts carefully.
items.exp: 'a child who was never corrected may become an adult who thinks he or she is never wrong and talks with total certainty'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

People are easily (A) ___ by confident speakers, but since confidence does not guarantee truth, we should (B) ___ information before accepting it.
choices: (A) persuaded — (B) spread
(A) bored — (B) check
(A) persuaded — (B) check
(A) ignored — (B) repeat
(A) corrected — (B) trust
items.exp: 'People tend to trust a statement much more when the speaker sounds certain'이지만 'check whether the facts are true'해야 한다고 했으니 persuaded와 check가 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (People tend to trust a statement much more when the speaker ___.)
choices: speaks slowly
sounds certain
is a close friend
uses difficult words
admits a mistake
items.exp: 바로 뒤에 'But sounding confident is not the same as being correct'라고 이어지니, 말하는 사람이 확신에 차 있을 때(sounds certain) 더 믿는다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: sounding confident is not the same as being [correct]
a successful person who is always [surrounded] by fans
we need to pause, check whether the facts are [true]
may say even very [wise] things in a perfectly confident voice
false information travels [fast]
items.exp: 너무 자만하게 된 사람이 자신 있는 목소리로 '아주 어리석은(silly)' 말을 할 수 있다는 흐름이라 wise는 맞지 않아요. 원문은 'say even very silly things'예요.

units.name: 29 Personal Principle
units.passage: Racing experts widely consider Mario Andretti to be one of the greatest race car drivers of all time. Once, someone asked him for his best piece of advice. He answered, "Never stare at the wall. Wherever your eyes look, your car will follow. At 200 miles per hour, you have to watch the track in front of you, since looking at an obstacle makes hitting it much more likely." This lesson is true not only on the racetrack but also in everyday life. If you pay attention to the criticism and negative words of difficult people, you will crash right into them. In our minds, we will drive ourselves toward anger, doubt about ourselves, or even feelings of failure. Negative messages can seem too powerful, especially when we allow them to decide what we look at. But if your attention stays on moving ahead, you can safely race past the walls in your way. When someone says something negative, use it as a signal to stay on your path. Life is too short to spend on pleasing difficult people. Watch the road, not the wall.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 다른 사람의 비난에 신경 쓰기보다 자신의 목표에 집중해야 한다.
비판을 꼼꼼히 분석해서 자신의 길을 바꿔야 한다.
까다로운 사람들을 기쁘게 하려고 노력해야 한다.
운전할 때는 속도를 줄이는 것이 가장 중요하다.
실패의 감정을 피하려면 도전하지 않아야 한다.
items.exp: 레이서의 조언을 삶에 적용해, 부정적인 말(벽)이 아니라 앞으로 나아가는 길(목표)에 시선을 두라고 주장하고 있어요.

items.q: Mario Andretti가 장애물을 보지 말라고 한 이유로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 장애물을 보면 속도가 너무 느려지기 때문에
장애물은 경기 규칙상 보면 안 되기 때문에
장애물을 보면 그것에 부딪힐 가능성이 훨씬 커지기 때문에
장애물보다 관중을 보는 것이 더 중요하기 때문에
장애물은 시속 200마일에서는 보이지 않기 때문에
items.exp: 장애물을 보면 그것을 칠 가능성이 훨씬 커진다(makes hitting it much more likely)고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 많은 전문가가 Mario Andretti를 최고의 레이서 중 한 명으로 여긴다.
Andretti는 눈이 가는 곳으로 차가 따라간다고 말했다.
글쓴이는 경주의 교훈이 일상생활에도 적용된다고 했다.
누군가의 부정적인 말을 자기 길을 지키라는 신호로 삼으라고 했다.
부정적인 말은 우리가 무엇을 볼지 결정하게 둘 때 힘이 약해진다.
items.exp: 부정적인 메시지는 우리가 무엇을 볼지 결정하게 둘 때 특히 너무 강하게 느껴질 수 있다(can seem too powerful)고 했어요.

items.q: 글에서 the wall이 비유적으로 가리키는 것으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: our goals for the future
the speed of a race car
advice from racing experts
criticism and negative words from others
the joy of winning a race
items.exp: 까다로운 사람들의 비판과 부정적인 말에 집중하면 그것에 부딪힌다고 했으므로, the wall은 다른 사람의 비난과 부정적인 말을 뜻해요.

items.q:
다음 문장과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
Life is [too short to spend] on pleasing difficult people.
choices: Life is short enough to spend on pleasing difficult people.
Life is so short that we can't spend it on pleasing difficult people.
Life is so short that we can spend it on pleasing difficult people.
Life is long, so we can spend it on pleasing difficult people.
Because life is short, we must please difficult people first.
items.exp: 'too ~ to-v'는 '너무 ~해서 v할 수 없다'는 뜻으로 'so ~ that ... can't'로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Drive at 200 Miles per Hour
The Life Story of Mario Andretti
Why Criticism Makes Us Better
Watch the Road, Not the Wall
Pleasing Difficult People Made Easy
items.exp: 레이서의 조언 'Never stare at the wall'을 삶에 적용해, 부정적인 말 대신 앞길에 집중하라는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, what can happen in our minds if we focus on negative words?
choices: We may become faster and safer drivers.
We may start to please everyone easily.
We may drive ourselves toward anger, self-doubt, or feelings of failure.
We may forget the advice of experts.
We may feel proud of our own path.
items.exp: 'In our minds, we will drive ourselves toward anger, doubt about ourselves, or even feelings of failure'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Just as a racer must keep his eyes on the (A) ___ rather than the wall, we should focus on moving forward instead of on others' (B) ___.
choices: (A) track — (B) praise
(A) wall — (B) criticism
(A) crowd — (B) advice
(A) speed — (B) success
(A) track — (B) criticism
items.exp: 'you have to watch the track in front of you'라는 조언을 'the criticism and negative words of difficult people'에 신경 쓰지 말라는 교훈으로 연결했으니 track과 criticism이 알맞아요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [you can safely race past the walls in your way]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (But if your attention stays on moving ahead, you can safely race past the walls in your way.)
choices: You can keep moving toward your goals without being hurt by negative words.
You can win every race you enter.
You can avoid driving on dangerous roads.
You can make difficult people like you.
You can build walls to protect yourself.
items.exp: 여기서 walls는 'the criticism and negative words of difficult people'을 뜻하므로, 앞에 집중하면 그런 말에 부딪히지 않고 지나갈 수 있다는 의미예요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: someone [asked] him for his best piece of advice
Racing experts widely consider Mario Andretti [being] one of the greatest
Wherever your eyes look, your car will [follow]
looking at an obstacle [makes] hitting it much more likely
when we allow them to [decide] what we look at
items.exp: 'consider + 목적어 + to be ~'는 '~을 …라고 여기다'라는 뜻으로 쓰여요. 원문은 'consider Mario Andretti to be one of the greatest'이므로 being은 틀려요.

units.name: 30 How to Respond
units.passage: In many situations, you might feel that you have to react at once. For instance, when someone asks you a question, you may feel pushed to give an answer immediately. Because of this, you can end up saying things that you feel sorry about later. If you never stop to think about your own emotions and needs, you might be allowing other people to make choices on your behalf. Pausing for a moment, however, gives you a chance to do several things. You can think carefully about the words you just heard, make sure you have really understood the speaker, and look inside yourself to discover what you really think, feel, and want right now. This helps you shape the situation on purpose, so you have a better chance of getting the result you hope for. It is useful to practice saying things like "That's interesting. Give me a second to think about it." or "This sounds important. Can you say that again?" Such words give you time to think and get ready.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 질문을 받으면 최대한 빨리 대답해야 한다.
다른 사람이 대신 결정하도록 맡기는 것이 편하다.
대화할 때는 상대의 말을 다시 묻지 않는 것이 예의다.
바로 대답하기보다 잠시 멈추고 자신의 생각과 감정을 살펴야 한다.
처음 떠오른 생각을 그대로 믿고 말해야 한다.
items.exp: 잠시 멈추면(Pausing for a moment) 상황을 이해하고 원하는 결과를 얻을 수 있다며 바로 반응하지 말라고 주장해요.

items.q: 글에서 언급된, 바로 반응할 때 생길 수 있는 문제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 상대방이 질문을 다시 하게 된다.
나중에 후회할 말을 하게 될 수 있다.
대화가 너무 길어지게 된다.
상대방의 말을 지나치게 분석하게 된다.
자신의 감정을 너무 많이 드러내게 된다.
items.exp: 바로 대답해야 한다는 압박 때문에 나중에 미안하게 느끼는 말을 하게 될 수 있다(end up saying things that you feel sorry about later)고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 잠시 멈추는 것은 원하는 결과를 얻을 가능성을 낮춘다.
질문을 받으면 즉시 대답해야 한다는 압박을 느낄 수 있다.
자신의 감정과 필요를 생각하지 않으면 남이 대신 선택하게 될 수 있다.
잠시 멈추면 상대를 제대로 이해했는지 확인할 수 있다.
"다시 말씀해 주시겠어요?" 같은 말은 생각할 시간을 준다.
items.exp: 잠시 멈추면 원하는 결과를 얻을 가능성이 더 커진다(a better chance of getting the result you hope for)고 했어요.

items.q:
밑줄 친 부분과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
This helps you shape the situation [on purpose], ...
choices: by accident
quickly
intentionally
angrily
without thinking
items.exp: on purpose는 '의도적으로, 일부러'라는 뜻으로 intentionally와 같아요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]의 의미로 알맞은 것은?
If you never stop [to think] about your own emotions and needs, ...
choices: 생각하는 것을 그만두기 위해
생각했던 것을 기억하기 위해
생각하지 않으려고 노력하기 위해
다른 사람이 생각하도록 강요하기 위해
(하던 일을) 멈추고 생각하기 위해
items.exp: 'stop + to-v'는 'v하기 위해 멈추다'라는 뜻이에요. 'stop + -ing'(~하는 것을 그만두다)와 구별해야 해요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Answer Questions Quickly
Take a Moment Before You Answer
Why Silence Ruins a Conversation
Let Others Decide for You
The Art of Asking Good Questions
items.exp: 'Pausing for a moment, however, gives you a chance to do several things'라며 바로 반응하지 말고 잠시 멈추라는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, what can pausing help you discover?
choices: What the speaker secretly wants from you.
How to end the conversation quickly.
Why other people make poor choices.
Which words the speaker will say next.
What you really think, feel, and want right now.
items.exp: 'look inside yourself to discover what you really think, feel, and want right now'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Reacting (A) ___ can lead to words we regret, so taking a brief pause lets us understand the speaker and respond in a way that (B) ___ the result we want.
choices: (A) instantly — (B) ruins
(A) slowly — (B) brings
(A) kindly — (B) delays
(A) instantly — (B) brings
(A) rarely — (B) blocks
items.exp: 'you have to react at once'라는 압박 때문에 후회할 말을 하게 되지만, 멈추면 'a better chance of getting the result you hope for'가 생긴다고 했으니 instantly와 brings가 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (In many situations, you might feel that you have to ___.)
choices: stay silent forever
agree with everyone
react at once
ask many questions
leave the room
items.exp: 이어서 'you may feel pushed to give an answer immediately'라고 예를 들었으니, 즉시 반응해야(react at once) 한다고 느낀다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: you can end up saying things that you feel [happy] about later
you may feel [pushed] to give an answer immediately
Pausing for a moment, however, gives you a [chance]
make sure you have really [understood] the speaker
Such words give you time to think and get [ready]
items.exp: 급하게 반응하면 나중에 '후회하는(sorry)' 말을 하게 된다는 부정적인 결과를 말하는 문맥이라 happy는 맞지 않아요. 원문은 'things that you feel sorry about later'예요.
